title: Stochastic Choice, Limited Attention, and Aggregation over Attributes
abstract: arXiv:2610.01333v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: We study an attribute-based model of stochastic choice in which attention to each attribute is limited, and characterize two choice rules within it. The Multiplicative Attention Rule (MAR) rewards an alternative only for the attributes on which it ranks first, combining attention to these multiplicatively across attributes; it captures choice deferral driven by the cognitive load of attending to `too many' attributes. The Additive Attention Rule (AAR) instead averages attention across attributes and credits an alternative by its full ordinal rank within the menu. This difference in aggregation is what separates the two rules behaviourally: AAR reproduces the Attraction Effect while holding the relevant attributes fixed across menus, something MAR can do only when the attribute set itself changes, though AAR, in turn, cannot accommodate the Compromise Effect. translated_title: 随机选择、有限注意力与属性聚合
translated_abstract: 我们研究了一个基于属性的随机选择模型，其中决策者对每个属性的注意力是有限的，并在该框架内刻画了两种选择规则。乘性注意力规则（MAR）仅根据备选方案在其上排名第一的属性给予其“奖励”，并将对这些属性的关注在多个属性间以乘法方式组合；该规则刻画了由关注“过多”属性所带来的认知负荷所导致的选择延迟行为。加性注意力规则（AAR）则对属性间的注意力取平均，并根据备选方案在菜单中的完整序数排名对其进行评价。这种聚合方式上的差异正是两种规则在行为上的分水岭：AAR能够在相关属性在各菜单间保持不变的情况下再现吸引效应，而这只有在属性集合本身发生变化时MAR才能做到；反过来，AAR却无法解释折中效应。两种规则均由基于可观测选择数据的公理加以刻画。
tldr: 该论文在注意力有限的基于属性随机选择模型中刻画了两种选择规则：乘性注意力规则（MAR）刻画由认知负荷导致的选择延迟，而加性注意力规则（AAR）在属性不变时能再现吸引效应但无法解释折中效应，二者的关键区别在于跨属性的注意力聚合方式。
en_tdlr: The paper characterizes two choice rules in an attribute-based stochastic choice model with limited attention: the Multiplicative Attention Rule captures cognitive-load-driven choice deferral, while the Additive Attention Rule reproduces the Attraction Effect (but not the Compromise Effect) with fixed attributes—the key distinction lying in how attention is aggregated across attributes.
